Theme

Travel & transport

vroom interjection

a car engine, in children’s talk

also vroom vroom, vroom-vroom

* our formation

Lucr. 6.581 (Lewis & Short s.v. fremō): of wind roaring in caves

* (our own formation) fremō, fremere, fremuī, fremitum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

roar, rumble (of an engine)

No ancient form of the sound is known. The classical verb for a low roar (Lewis & Short: “to make a low roaring”), of wind, sea and beasts, applied by us to the engine.

Other words

  • * (our own formation) fremitus, fremitūs m. — the roar of the engine

    noun, fourth declension · also used · * our formation · Cic. Tusc. 5.116 (Lewis & Short s.v. fremitus): of the murmuring sea · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Audīn' autoraedam frementem?

    Do you hear the car roaring?composed

See also car, toy car, car horn.

SourcesLewis & Short: fremo · Lewis & Short: fremitus

No ancient form of the sound is known; the uses are ours, on the classical verb.
